pr_title: ActionText::Content - Strip `content` attribute if it is empty
pr_body:
### Motivation / Background

Images and other attachments added to a rich text area aren't being displayed in the editor when you go back to edit the record again.

Fixes: https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/52233

### Detail

This Pull Request makes it so that if the `action-text-attachment` element contains an empty `content` attribute, that attribute will be stripped out during the rendering of attachments.

### Additional information

None

Before submitting the PR make sure the following are checked:

* [x] This Pull Request is related to one change. Unrelated changes should be opened in separate PRs.
* [x] Commit message has a detailed description of what changed and why. If this PR fixes a related issue include it in the commit message. Ex: `[Fix #issue-number]`
* [x] Tests are added or updated if you fix a bug or add a feature.
* [x] CHANGELOG files are updated for the changed libraries if there is a behavior change or additional feature. Minor bug fixes and documentation changes should not be included.

issue_context.title: [ActionText] Editor didn't load attachments after saving and opening edit again.
issue_context.body:
Hi! I am expecting this strange bug on fresh new rails application I hope someone could help me. ### Steps to reproduce 1. `rails new my-blog -d postgresql`. 2. `rails action_text:install` 3. `rails g scaffold Post name:string title:string content:text` 4. Adds tag at Model ```ruby class Post < ApplicationRecord has_rich_text :content end ``` 5. Add tag at _form ```ruby <%= form_with(model: post) do |form| %> ...
<%= form.label :content, style: "display: block" %> <%= form.rich_text_area :content %>
... <% end %> ``` 6. Test it https://github.com/rails/rails/assets/63271570/0a142613-8010-41d3-bb65-a44228437076 ### Expected behavior It used render the edit after save just in the past (1 year ago at least) ### Actual behavior It didn't render the attachments thumbs and not even the label for .zips for example. ### System configuration **Rails version**: Rails 7.1.3.4 **Ruby version**: ruby 3.3.3 (2024-06-12 revision f1c7b6f435) [x86_64-linux]
comments:
@joaovictor-local This should be fixed on the stable-7-1 branch. See https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/52127 and https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/52093.
@rafaelfranca could we get a 7.1.3.5 release to fix this in an offical release?
I was just coming to file an issue with the same repro steps. Would be really nice to get a bug fix release out asap.

I'm not entirely sure that the change from #52093 fixes this.

In a brand new rails app I added this initializer to monkey patch in the change from #52093:

```ruby
# config/initializers/action_text_bug_fix.rb

require "action_text/content"

module ActionText
  class Content
    def render_attachments(**options, &block)
      puts "*" * 300
      puts "calling monkey patched render_attachments"
      puts "*" * 300
      content = fragment.replace(ActionText::Attachment.tag_name) do |node|
        if node.key? "content"
          node["content"] = sanitize_content_attachment(node["content"])
        end
        block.call(attachment_for_node(node, **options))
      end
      self.class.new(content, canonicalize: false)
    end
  end
end
```

I've verified that my monkey patched version of `render_attachments` is being called when I visit the edit page, but the image still isn't showing up in the editor.

It looks like there's just no `img` tag included in the generated markup on the edit page:

![CleanShot 2024-07-05 at 11 03 26](https://github.com/rails/rails/assets/58702/4f631d97-1fe0-4e4c-a392-0d5f3dbe8de3)

On the show page there is an `img` tag inside the `figure` element:

![CleanShot 2024-07-05 at 11 04 43](https://github.com/rails/rails/assets/58702/d35ba3de-7cd1-458c-b5f5-a9ba6a3811ac)

I've also experimented with a few different unreleased versions via `github:` installation. And none of them seem to fix the problem. These are all _without_ the monkey patch mentioned above.

### `branch: "7-1-stable"`

```ruby
gem "rails", github: "rails/rails", branch: "7-1-stable"
```

In `7-1-stable` the images are now broken on the `index` and `show` pages, and are still completely missing on the `edit` page.


![CleanShot 2024-07-05 at 11 50 35](https://github.com/rails/rails/assets/58702/2d8f7fe7-7135-483d-a875-4da28b632920)

### `branch: "7-2-stable"`

```ruby
gem "rails", github: "rails/rails", branch: "7-2-stable"
```

In `7-2-stable` the images work as expected on the `index` and `show` pages, but are still completely missing on the `edit` page.

### `branch: "main"`

```ruby
gem "rails", github: "rails/rails", branch: "main"
```

In `main` (which gets me `8.0.0.alpha`) the images work as expected on the `index` and `show` pages, but are still completely missing on the `edit` page.

I was able to get things working with this modified monkey patch. The problem is that the fix in #52093 only checks whether the `content` **key** is _present_, but it doesn't check whether that key has a non-empty **value**. When the key is there with an empty value we should strip it out.

```ruby
# config/initializers/action_text_bug_fix.rb

require "action_text/content"

module ActionText
  class Content
    def render_attachments(**options, &block)
      content = fragment.replace(ActionText::Attachment.tag_name) do |node|
        if node.key?("content") && node["content"].present?
          node["content"] = sanitize_content_attachment(node["content"])
        elsif node.key?("content")
          node.remove_attribute("content")
        end
        block.call(attachment_for_node(node, **options))
      end
      self.class.new(content, canonicalize: false)
    end
  end
end
```

This works, tyvm!

@jagthedrummer I'm wondering if the fix is not working for you because invalid blank `content` values were created during the window when you were running 7.1.3.4? The 7-1 stable branch seems to work for us but we explicitly cleaned up the "bad data" caused by the original sanitizer issue: https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/52127#issuecomment-2216256859

@swanson I don't _think_ that's the case, I'm pretty sure that I was creating new records each time I tried a new branch. But I wouldn't swear to it since it's been a month and a half since I did the tests.

review_comments: Could you add a test to test no content attribute is added if it is empty after sanitization? As this is a more special case it would probably make more sense to move it under the other newly added test. ```suggestion test "removes content attribute if it's value is empty after sanitization" do html = '' trix_html = '' assert_equal trix_html, content_from_html(html).to_trix_html.strip end ```
Maybe this test is redundant now?

@p8 I'm not entirely sure. On the one hand it does seem to test for the same thing as the test where we have `content=""`, but on the other hand maybe it's good to test "missing" and "empty" as separate cases?

Anyway, sorry for the delay, but I just merged your other suggestions and did a little clean up as a result of the merge. Please let me know if you want me to remove the possibly-redundant test.
